issue.title: Build fails when building from a git worktree: submodule git metadata is outside the container bind-mount (breaks scapy version derivation)

failure.body:
## Description

Building from a **`git worktree`** of `sonic-buildimage` (instead of a full standalone clone) fails because the build containers only bind-mount the worktree directory, not the parent repository's `.git` directory where worktree/submodule git metadata actually lives. As a result, any in-container `git` command run against a submodule fails with `fatal: not a git repository`, which silently breaks version-string derivation for at least the `scapy` python wheel and aborts the build.

There are valid use cases for worktrees (e.g. building multiple branches/commits from a single bare-ish clone without re-downloading ~GBs of submodules per branch), so it would be nice for the build system to support, or at least clearly document/detect, worktree mode.

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
# Existing full clone with submodules
cd /data/sonic-buildimage          # origin = sonic-net/sonic-buildimage

# Create a worktree for master and build the VS image from it
git worktree add /data/sonic-buildimage-master -b master-latest
cd /data/sonic-buildimage-master
git fetch origin master && git reset --hard origin/master
git submodule update --init --recursive

make configure PLATFORM=vs
make SONIC_BUILD_JOBS=4 target/sonic-vs.img.gz
```

## Observed result

Build fails at the `scapy` wheel step:

```
Created wheel for scapy: filename=scapy-2026.6.20-py3-none-any.whl ...
Building Wheels package target/python-wheels/bookworm/scapy-2.6.1.dev0-py3-none-any.whl
mv: cannot stat 'src/scapy/dist/scapy-2.6.1.dev0-py3-none-any.whl': No such file or directory
[  FAIL LOG END  ] [ target/python-wheels/bookworm/scapy-2.6.1.dev0-py3-none-any.whl ]
make: *** [slave.mk:1081: target/python-wheels/bookworm/scapy-2.6.1.dev0-py3-none-any.whl] Error 1
```

The whole build is also spammed with thousands of:

```
fatal: not a git repository: /data/sonic-buildimage/.git/worktrees/sonic-buildimage-master/...
```

## Root cause

In a worktree, a submodule's `.git` is a **pointer file**, not a directory. For example `src/scapy/.git` contains:

```
gitdir: ../../../sonic-buildimage/.git/worktrees/sonic-buildimage-master/modules/src/scapy
```

The build container only bind-mounts the worktree dir into `/sonic`:

```
docker run ... -v /data/sonic-buildimage-master:/sonic -w /sonic ... sonic-slave-bookworm ...
```

So inside the container that gitdir resolves to
`/sonic/src/scapy/../../../sonic-buildimage/.git/worktrees/...`, i.e. it points **outside** the mount, to a path that does not exist in the container. Every in-container `git` call against a submodule therefore returns `rc=128 / fatal: not a git repository`.

`scapy`'s version logic (`scapy/__init__.py::_version()`) tries, in order: `SCAPY_VERSION` env → `scapy/VERSION` file → git-archive subst → **`git describe`** → **date fallback** (`strftime('%Y.%m.%d')`). The only method that yields the pinned `2.6.1.dev0` is `git describe`, and it is wrapped in `except Exception: pass`. With git unreachable in-container it falls through to the date, producing `scapy-2026.6.20-...whl`, while `rules/scapy.mk` expects `scapy-2.6.1.dev0-...whl` → `mv` fails.

This was confirmed with instrumentation inside the in-container build:

```
SONIC-SCAPY-DIAG: enter _version_from_git_describe pkgdir='/sonic/src/scapy/scapy' parent='/sonic/src/scapy' dotgit_exists=True
SONIC-SCAPY-DIAG: git FAILED rc=128 cmd='git describe --tags --always --long' cwd='/sonic/src/scapy/scapy'
   stderr='fatal: not a git repository: /sonic/src/scapy/../../../sonic-buildimage/.git/worktrees/sonic-buildimage-master/modules/src/scapy'
SONIC-SCAPY-DIAG: Method3(git describe) FAIL CalledProcessError: ... exit status 128.
SONIC-SCAPY-DIAG: falling through to DATE fallback (THIS IS THE BUG)
```

Note `dotgit_exists=True` — so the existing patch `src/scapy.patch/0001-Fix-version-string-generation-when-scapy-is-a-submod.patch` (which only removes an `os.path.isdir('.git')` precheck) does **not** help here; the failure is one level deeper, in `git describe` itself.

`scapy` is just the first casualty; any build step that shells out to `git` in a submodule under a worktree is exposed to the same class of failure.

## Expected result

Building from a `git worktree` should either work, or fail fast with a clear message, rather than silently producing wrong version strings deep into the build.

## Possible fixes / mitigations

- **Mount the parent `.git`/common dir** into the build containers when the source tree is a worktree (e.g. also `-v <common-git-dir>:<same-path>`), or rewrite gitdir pointers to in-container paths.
- **Make version derivation robust to unreachable git** — e.g. honor `SCAPY_VERSION` from the build env for the scapy wheel (verified workaround: `SCAPY_VERSION=2.6.1.dev0` makes `_version()` return the pinned version regardless of git), and similarly for any other component that derives versions from git at build time.
- **Detect worktree mode** in `make configure` / `Makefile.work` and emit a clear warning/guard if it is unsupported.

## Workaround

- Build from a regular full `git clone` (self-contained `.git/`) instead of a worktree, **or**
- Export `SCAPY_VERSION=2.6.1.dev0` (matching `rules/scapy.mk`) into the build environment.

## Environment

- Repo: `sonic-net/sonic-buildimage` master @ `be9722abb`
- Source tree: a `git worktree` (`/data/sonic-buildimage-master`, branch `master-latest` tracking `origin/master`) of a full clone at `/data/sonic-buildimage`
- Target: `target/sonic-vs.img.gz` / `target/docker-sonic-vs.gz`, `PLATFORM=vs`, bookworm slave

resolution.title: [build] Support building from a git worktree
resolution.description:
#### Why I did it

Building sonic-buildimage from a `git worktree` (instead of a normal clone) fails, because in-container `git` breaks. This fixes #28002.

In a worktree, `$(PWD)/.git` is a *file* pointing into the parent repo's git dir, and the build only bind-mounts the worktree directory (`$(PWD):/sonic`). Two things then break inside the slave container:

1. **Submodule git / work-tree detection.** Each submodule's `.git` pointer and its gitdir's `core.worktree` back-reference resolve to paths **outside** the `$(PWD):/sonic` mount, so in-container submodule git (e.g. `src/scapy`, `src/sonic-frr`) fails with `fatal: not a git repository` (Error 128), and tools like `stg` fail with `Not inside a git worktree`. This breaks at least:
   - the **scapy** wheel (scapy derives its version from in-container git via `src/scapy.patch/0001-Fix-version-string-generation-when-scapy-is-a-submod.patch`; when git fails it falls back to a date version and the expected `scapy-2.6.1.dev0-...whl` is never produced), and
   - the **FRR** deb (`src/sonic-frr` runs `git`, `stg`, and `gbp dch` in-container).

2. **Image version string.** `git worktree add` records the **top-level** worktree `.git` pointer as an **absolute** gitdir path into the parent repo (e.g. `gitdir: /abs/parent/.git/worktrees/<wt>`), unlike submodule `.git` pointers which are written relative. That absolute host path does not exist at the same location inside the container, so the in-container `git` used by `slave.mk` to compute `SONIC_IMAGE_VERSION` returns empty. The empty version then produces an invalid Docker tag and the build fails late, e.g.:
   ```
   docker tag docker-macsec:.0- ...
   invalid reference format: "docker-macsec:.0-" is not a valid repository/tag
   ```
   so the full image (`target/sonic-vs.img.gz`) is never produced.

#### How I did it

All changes are in `Makefile.work` and apply **only** when building from a worktree. For a normal clone the detection is a no-op (the extra mounts are empty, the workdir stays `/sonic`, and the pointer fixup is empty), so nothing changes.

1. **Bind-mount the parent git dir + align the workdir.** Additionally bind-mount:
   - the parent repo's common git dir at the absolute path the worktree's `.git` pointers reference inside the container, and
   - the worktree tree at its parent-relative basename path, so each submodule gitdir's `core.worktree` back-reference resolves onto the real tree,

   and run the build from that basename path (`DOCKER_BUILDER_WORKDIR`) so git's inferred work tree matches the build working directory. `/sonic` stays mounted for paths that reference it directly. Both mounts are read-write because package builds such as FRR write to the git dir.

2. **Normalize the top-level `.git` pointer to a relative gitdir.** As the first step of the in-container build command, rewrite the worktree's top-level `.git` pointer from the absolute parent path to the equivalent **relative** gitdir (the same form `git` already uses for submodule pointers — see the `init` target's `git submodule foreach ... realpath --relative-to=.`). A relative gitdir resolves correctly **both** on the host and inside the container, because the worktree directory keeps the same relative relationship to the parent `.git` in either location. This lets `slave.mk` compute a non-empty `SONIC_IMAGE_VERSION` and produces a valid Docker tag.

The helper variables are deliberately named `SONIC_WT_*` (not `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_COMMON_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE`), because those are environment variable names git itself honors and would otherwise leak into child git invocations.

This assumes the worktree is created with the standard `git worktree add ../<name>` layout (a sibling of the parent repo).

#### How to verify it

From a worktree of sonic-buildimage:
```
git worktree add ../sonic-buildimage-wt -b some-branch
cd ../sonic-buildimage-wt
make init
make configure PLATFORM=vs
make SONIC_BUILD_JOBS=4 target/sonic-vs.img.gz
```
Before this change the build aborts at the scapy wheel (`mv: cannot stat '.../scapy-2.6.1.dev0-...whl'`), then at the trixie FRR deb (`fatal: not a git repository` / `stg ... Not inside a git worktree`), and — once those are mounted — late at the Docker tag step with an empty version (`docker tag docker-macsec:.0-` / `not a valid repository/tag`).

With this change, building from a worktree:
- produces `scapy-2.6.1.dev0-py3-none-any.whl`,
- produces `frr_10.5.4-sonic-0_amd64.deb` (plus `frr-dbgsym`, `frr-snmp`, `frr-snmp-dbgsym`),
- resolves a non-empty `SONIC_IMAGE_VERSION` so the Docker images tag correctly, and
- builds `target/sonic-vs.img.gz` end-to-end.

Normal (non-worktree) builds are unaffected.

Fixes #28002
